liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): The jam evolution exemplifies the band's capabilities in the early 1980s; Jerry shreds every song, but Bird Song is the standout with superb interplay [11][19]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): The opener was so precise it resembled a mid-set or second-set start [10]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Garcia’s guitar danced atop the strong backing, making the performance smokin’ hot [10]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): One of the most intense versions, with the crowd getting amped up [12]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): The transition to Saint Of Circumstance is described as out of space [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-03-03.139736.fob.beyer.m88.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 156 min [1]
- **gd1981-03-03.nak700.wagner.miller.90473.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 165 min; rated 3.82/5 by 11 [4]. Said about its sound: The audience recording is described as unreal, surpassing the need for a soundboard [14]
- **gd1981-03-03.sbd.digitalrbb.miller.112777.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 156 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: The soundboard has a little background hiss but is otherwise good sounding [15]
- **gd1981-03-03.139735.fob.beyer.m88.streeter.miller.clugston.flac1644**: audience recording; 20 songs; 156 min [2]

## Around the show

- The crowd’s stunned reaction at the end hinted at the show’s quality [10]
- The venue resembles Barton Hall, being slightly smaller and more ornate [18]
- Cleveland brought out the best in the band, making the first set solid [12]
- The audience recording is more enjoyable than the board for this listener [17]
- The performance is considered better than the March 7 Cole Field House show [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-03-03.139736.fob.beyer.m88.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Beyer M88 > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell MX90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi CR-7A) > Tascam… [1]
- **gd1981-03-03.nak700.wagner.miller.90473.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 (With Bass EQ) -> Cassette Master (Sony D5M/Maxell DXLIIS/Dolby B) D [4]. Also: Recorded front row center balcony using Sennheiser 421 mics to cassette master; Bob Wagner lent his masters for the front-of-house recording [4]
- **gd1981-03-03.sbd.digitalrbb.miller.112777.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [6]
- **gd1981-03-03.139735.fob.beyer.m88.streeter.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Beyer M88 > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell MX90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi CR-7A) > Tascam… [2]
